correctness.rationale: An additive functional on \(\Delta_{d-1}	imes\Delta_{e-1}\) has scores \(p_i+q_j\). After its unique maximum, the second largest score must change only one factor, while every ordered row-sharing or column-sharing pair is realizable by separating the corresponding score gaps. The source vertex criterion therefore gives exactly the two occupation-vector families displayed in the theorem. Each has squared norm \(1+lpha^2+ eta^2\), block sums \(1\) and \(1\), and hence one common distance from the row-column uniform point. The cyclic same-row vertices average exactly to that point; the mean squared-distance identity then proves the common sphere is minimum enclosing and uniquely centered.

value.rationale: Lineup polytopes of products of simplices are a recent geometry motivated by quantum marginal problems, with substantial work devoted to their vertex and facet complexity. The two-lineup case has a natural physical and combinatorial meaning as the weighted occupation of the two highest product states. The theorem gives a closed realization-sensitive metric invariant for every pair of simplex dimensions and every admissible weight vector, proves that all vertices are active contacts, and supplies a sparse explicit optimality certificate. This is a family-wide exact geometric classification rather than a low-dimensional table or arbitrary slice.
